sections.section_title: LPDMA transfer in peripheral flow-control mode
sections.text_helper: Section 14.4.14 "LPDMA transfer in peripheral flow-control mode" in chapter 14 (Low-power direct memory access controller (LPDMA)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 417.
sections.section_content:
A peripheral with the peripheral flow-control mode feature can decide to early terminate an
LPDMA block transfer, provided that the allocated channel is implemented with this feature
(seeSection14.3.6).
If the related LPDMA channel x is also programmed in peripheral flow-control mode
(LPDMA_CxTR2.PFREQ = 1):
• The LPDMA block transfer starts as follows:
– If LPDMA_CxBR1.BNDT[15:0]?0, the programmed value is internally taken into
account by the LPDMA hardware.
– If LPDMA_CxBR1.BNDT[15:0] = 0, the LPDMA hardware internally considers a
64-Kbyte value for the maximum source block size to be transferred.
• The LPDMA block transfer is completed as soon as the first occurrence of one of the
following condition occurs:
– when LPDMA_CxBR1.BNDT[15:0] = 0
– when the peripheral early terminates the block. The complete transfer event is
generated if programmed, depending on LPDMA_CxTR2 (seeLPDMA channel x
transfer register 2 (LPDMA_CxTR2)). Then the software can read the current
number of transferred bytes from the source (LPDMA_CxBR1.BNDT[15:0]),
and/or read the current source or destination address of the buffer in memory
(LPDMA_CxSAR[31:0] or LPDMA_CxDAR[31:0]).
